title: Relay queue overflow or SourceBuffer error after playback starts leaves the UI in watching/relay state with a frozen stream
test: tests/browser/media-flow.spec.mjs: 'a relay viewer whose stream turns unreadable is told why, gets Watch Stream back and can watch again' and 'a relay start that falls behind before it plays reports that, not a generic cleanup error' (chromium); tests/relayAppendQueue.test.js: 'an append that fails while the browser parses it ends relay playback, and its updateend is not taken as success', 'the MediaSource ending or closing under the player ends relay playback', 'an append that is due while the MediaSource is not open ends relay playback instead of waiting', 'more chunks or bytes than the limits allow end relay playback with the fell-behind message', 'a closed queue, or one whose attempt is no longer current, ignores late events and reports nothing', 'WatchView appends relay media only through the queue and ends failed relay playback visibly'
proof: Browser repro 1: a playing tunnel-origin relay viewer's next append reaches the real SourceBuffer as zero bytes of the same length (an init-script wrapper on SourceBuffer.prototype.appendBuffer). Chromium fires 'error' on the SourceBuffer and ends the MediaSource (probe: watch-TASK-089-mse-probe.cjs.txt, output watch-TASK-089-mse-probe-output.txt; the same for WebM and MP4, after which Chromium also sets video.error 3 and refuses further appends). On the unchanged code (lane/watch 98e7a63, run-e2e.cjs on the lane's own ports, scratchpad watch-TASK-089-before-e2e.txt) no alert appeared within 10 s and the page snapshot still showed 'Compatibility relay mode active (higher latency).' with Mute/Fullscreen/Leave and no Watch Stream: the error listener only cleared appendingLock and processQueue returned early on the ended MediaSource. Browser repro 2: a direct viewer whose WebRTC cannot connect (relay-only ICE, no TURN) falls back to the relay; its appends never finish and every media-chunk frame is delivered 30 times, so the queue overflows before anything buffers. Unchanged code: the alert read 'Relay playback was cleaned up before media buffered.' (cleanupRelayAttempt settled the start with its generic error before the overflow, and handleWatch's catch replaced the overflow message with it). After the fix both pass: the first shows 'The browser could not read the relay stream, so relay playback must be restarted.', no relay status, Watch Stream enabled, video src '' and no srcObject, relayViewerCount 0; Watch Stream then plays the relay again; a MediaSource closed under the player (video.load() without src) ends playback the same way with 'The browser closed the relay stream...'. The second shows 'Relay playback fell behind and must be restarted.' with no playback mode and relayViewerCount/mediasoupConsumerCount 0. Fix: failRelayGeneration settles the start with the specific failure first, then cleans up the attempt (listeners, queue, waits rejected with the failure) and releases its relay claim; before playback is established startRelayPlayback rejects with that failure (assertRelayRunning after every await), after it failRelayGeneration runs cleanupPlayback, setWatching(false), setPlaybackMode('') and setError(failure.message); setFallbackState('error') is gone from this path. src/lib/relayAppendQueue.mjs listens for the SourceBuffer's 'error' and the MediaSource's 'sourceended'/'sourceclose' (and treats a MediaSource that is not open when an append is due as closed); close() runs in the attempt's cleanup before cleanupPlayback tears the MediaSource down, and events are ignored once the attempt is no longer current. Unit tests: they failed on the unchanged code with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND (new module), the source-level one with 'every relay append goes through relayAppendQueue' (watch-TASK-089-before-unit.txt); 13/13 after. Verification: whole media-flow spec 21/21 (watch-TASK-089-after-media-flow.txt), the three new tests plus the two generation-switch tests 15/15 with --repeat-each=3 (watch-TASK-089-after-repeat.txt); npm run lint and typecheck clean; npm test 1431/1431.

title: Relay append failures silently discard required media bytes
test: tests/browser/media-flow.spec.mjs: 'a relay viewer whose SourceBuffer is full evicts and appends the same chunk again; any other refused append ends playback visibly' (chromium); tests/relayAppendQueue.test.js: 'a chunk leaves the queue, and its bytes the count, only once its append has finished', 'a full SourceBuffer frees what is more than 10 s behind the playhead and appends the same chunk again', 'a SourceBuffer still full after its eviction ends relay playback with the buffer message', 'a full SourceBuffer with nothing 10 s behind the playhead ends relay playback at once', 'an append the SourceBuffer refuses for another reason ends relay playback with that reason', 'a flush for a new generation drops the chunk being appended without taking its aborted updateend for the next one', 'bootstrap chunks put in front are appended before the live ones, in order'
proof: Browser repro: a playing relay viewer (past 11 s of media) gets one QuotaExceededError DOMException from appendBuffer (init-script wrapper; it records the refused chunk and SourceBuffer.remove calls). On the unchanged code (watch-TASK-089-before-e2e.txt) the test failed at 'the refused chunk is appended again': expected 1, received 0 after 15 s; processQueue had shifted the chunk and deducted its bytes before appendBuffer, and the catch only logged, so the chunk was lost and later chunks went on. After the fix: one remove(0, t) with 0 < t <= currentTime - 10, the same chunk object is appended again, the video keeps advancing, no alert, relay status still shown; a following InvalidStateError from appendBuffer ends playback with 'The browser refused relay media (InvalidStateError), so relay playback must be restarted.', Watch Stream back, video src cleared, relayViewerCount 0. Fix: src/lib/relayAppendQueue.mjs peeks the head chunk and removes it (and its bytes) only on the updateend of its own append; a chunk flushed for a new recorder generation meanwhile is not removed twice, and the aborted append's updateend does not count for the next chunk. A QuotaExceededError evicts sourceBuffer.remove(0, currentTime - 10) and retries the same chunk once; with nothing that old, a failed remove, or a second QuotaExceededError for the chunk, playback ends with 'The browser has no room left to buffer the relay stream, so relay playback must be restarted.'. Any other appendBuffer exception ends playback with its name in the message. In every failure case nothing after the failed chunk is appended. The unit tests use a fake SourceBuffer that throws while updating, like the real one. MAX_QUEUE_CHUNKS (240) and MAX_QUEUE_BYTES (24 MB) are unchanged; the chunk being appended now counts toward them until its append ends. Media-init generation filtering, the flush on a new generation and the bootstrap order are unchanged (the check-19 generation-switch tests pass 3 of 3). Verification as for C-d20f555bcf10: media-flow 21/21, repeats 15/15, unit 13/13, lint and typecheck clean, npm test 1431/1431.
